entries.title: I Chronicles 7:1
segments: ¶The sons of Issachar [were] Tola, Puah, Jashub, and Shimron-four [in all].

entries.title: I Chronicles 7:2
segments: The sons of Tola [were] Uzzi, Rephaiah, Jeriel, Jahmai, Jibsam, and Shemuel, heads of their father's house. [The sons] of Tola [were] mighty men of valor in their generations; their number in the days of David [was] twenty-two thousand six hundred.

entries.title: I Chronicles 7:3
segments: The son of Uzzi [was] Izrahiah, and the sons of Izrahiah [were] Michael, Obadiah, Joel, and Ishiah. All five of them [were] chief men.

entries.title: I Chronicles 7:4
segments: And with them, by their generations, according to their fathers' houses, [were] thirty-six thousand troops ready for war; for they had many wives and sons.

entries.title: I Chronicles 7:5
segments: Now their brethren among all the families of Issachar [were] mighty men of valor, listed by their genealogies, eighty-seven thousand in all.

entries.title: I Chronicles 7:6
segments: [The sons] of Benjamin [were] Bela, Becher, and Jediael-three [in all].

entries.title: I Chronicles 7:7
segments: The sons of Bela were Ezbon, Uzzi, Uzziel, Jerimoth, and Iri-five [in all]. They [were] heads of [their] fathers' houses, and they were listed by their genealogies, twenty-two thousand and thirty-four mighty men of valor.

entries.title: I Chronicles 7:8
segments: The sons of Becher [were] Zemirah, Joash, Eliezer, Elioenai, Omri, Jerimoth, Abijah, Anathoth, and Alemeth. All these [are] the sons of Becher.

entries.title: I Chronicles 7:9
segments: And they were recorded by genealogy according to their generations, heads of their fathers' houses, twenty thousand two hundred mighty men of valor.

entries.title: I Chronicles 7:10
segments: The son of Jediael [was] Bilhan, and the sons of Bilhan [were] Jeush, Benjamin, Ehud, Chenaanah, Zethan, Tharshish, and Ahishahar.

entries.title: I Chronicles 7:11
segments: All these sons of Jediael [were] heads of their fathers' houses; [there were] seventeen thousand two hundred mighty men of valor fit to go out for war [and] battle.

entries.title: I Chronicles 7:12
segments: Shuppim and Huppim [were] the sons of Ir, [and] Hushim [was] the son of Aher.

entries.title: I Chronicles 7:13
segments: The sons of Naphtali [were] Jahziel, Guni, Jezer, and Shallum, the sons of Bilhah.

entries.title: I Chronicles 7:14
segments: The descendants of Manasseh: his Syrian concubine bore him Machir the father of Gilead, the father of Asriel.

entries.title: I Chronicles 7:15
segments: Machir took as his wife [the sister] of Huppim and Shuppim, whose name [was] Maachah. The name of [Gilead's] grandson [was] Zelophehad, but Zelophehad begot only daughters.

entries.title: I Chronicles 7:16
segments: (Maachah the wife of Machir bore a son, and she called his name Peresh. The name of his brother [was] Sheresh, and his sons [were] Ulam and Rakem.

entries.title: I Chronicles 7:17
segments: The son of Ulam [was] Bedan.) These [were] the descendants of Gilead the son of Machir, the son of Manasseh.

entries.title: I Chronicles 7:18
segments: His sister Hammoleketh bore Ishhod, Abiezer, and Mahlah.

entries.title: I Chronicles 7:19
segments: And the sons of Shemida were Ahian, Shechem, Likhi, and Aniam.

entries.title: I Chronicles 7:20
segments: ¶The sons of Ephraim [were] Shuthelah, Bered his son, Tahath his son, Eladah his son, Tahath his son,

entries.title: I Chronicles 7:21
segments: Zabad his son, Shuthelah his son, and Ezer and Elead. The men of Gath who were born in [that] land killed [them] because they came down to take away their cattle.

entries.title: I Chronicles 7:22
segments: Then Ephraim their father mourned many days, and his brethren came to comfort him.

entries.title: I Chronicles 7:23
segments: And when he went in to his wife, she conceived and bore a son; and he called his name Beriah, because tragedy had come upon his house.

entries.title: I Chronicles 7:24
segments: Now his daughter [was] Sheerah, who built Lower and Upper Beth Horon and Uzzen Sheerah;

entries.title: I Chronicles 7:25
segments: and Rephah [was] his son, [as well] as Resheph, and Telah his son, Tahan his son,

entries.title: I Chronicles 7:26
segments: Laadan his son, Ammihud his son, Elishama his son,

entries.title: I Chronicles 7:27
segments: Nun his son, and Joshua his son.

entries.title: I Chronicles 7:28
segments: Now their possessions and dwelling places [were] Bethel and its towns: to the east Naaran, to the west Gezer and its towns, and Shechem and its towns, as far as Ayyah and its towns;

entries.title: I Chronicles 7:29
segments: and by the borders of the children of Manasseh [were] Beth Shean and its towns, Taanach and its towns, Megiddo and its towns, Dor and its towns. In these dwelt the children of Joseph, the son of Israel.

entries.title: I Chronicles 7:30
segments: The sons of Asher [were] Imnah, Ishvah, Ishvi, Beriah, and their sister Serah.

entries.title: I Chronicles 7:31
segments: The sons of Beriah [were] Heber and Malchiel, who was the father of Birzaith.

entries.title: I Chronicles 7:32
segments: And Heber begot Japhlet, Shomer, Hotham, and their sister Shua.

entries.title: I Chronicles 7:33
segments: The sons of Japhlet [were] Pasach, Bimhal, and Ashvath. These [were] the children of Japhlet.

entries.title: I Chronicles 7:34
segments: The sons of Shemer [were] Ahi, Rohgah, Jehubbah, and Aram.

entries.title: I Chronicles 7:35
segments: And the sons of his brother Helem [were] Zophah, Imna, Shelesh, and Amal.

entries.title: I Chronicles 7:36
segments: The sons of Zophah [were] Suah, Harnepher, Shual, Beri, Imrah,

entries.title: I Chronicles 7:37
segments: Bezer, Hod, Shamma, Shilshah, Jithran, and Beera.

entries.title: I Chronicles 7:38
segments: The sons of Jether [were] Jephunneh, Pispah, and Ara.

entries.title: I Chronicles 7:39
segments: The sons of Ulla [were] Arah, Haniel, and Rizia.

entries.title: I Chronicles 7:40
segments: All these [were] the children of Asher, heads of [their] fathers' houses, choice men, mighty men of valor, chief leaders. And they were recorded by genealogies among the army fit for battle; their number [was] twenty-six thousand.
